ladder.ask: an honest written testimonial I can quote, said plainly as a founding client, and permission to show the photos in my portfolio
ladder.step_up: After 3 founding clients new clients pay the full menu price.
ladder.reviews_rule: Ask for Google reviews separately, never tied to the discount (Google Maps content policy).

promise: Your edited photos are in your online gallery within 3 days of the shoot. If a photo isn't right, I edit it again free, and if weather or a closure moves the shoot, the new date costs nothing.
job_checklist: Two days before: confirm the date, the quiet hour, who will be there and the shot list in writing.
Check the place at that time of day: where the light comes from, what to move out of frame, where to park.
Shoot day: charged batteries, empty cards, the shot list; a signed release from anyone recognizable you may show in your own portfolio or ads.
Back up every card before you format it.
Cull and edit; deliver the gallery by the promised date (24 hours for listing photos), with file names that say what each photo shows.
After delivery: send the after-delivery message, help put the best ones on their website and Google profile, and offer the monthly session.

objections.says: We can just use a phone.
objections.answer: Fine for daily posts; for portraits, headshots and listings, show side-by-side light, posing and editing.

objections.says: Why does a one-hour session cost that much?
objections.answer: The price covers planning, the shoot, editing time and delivery; list the edited images and gallery included.

objections.says: Do we get all the photos?
objections.answer: Promise a number of finished, edited images and offer more as an add-on.

objections.says: Can we use the photos for our business and ads?
objections.answer: Yes, under a written usage license; you keep the copyright unless the contract says otherwise.
Agree a weather plan and backup date in the contract.
Short session, guided posing, and a look at the first few frames on the back of the camera.

licenses.check: No photography license exists in any state, but most cities want a business license, and a DBA if you use a business name.

sources.says: Licenses and permits depend on business activity and location; local governments set registration, licensing and permitting rules; research your own state, county and city; some licenses expire and must be renewed.
No photography license is required in any state; you need standard business registration and a local business license where required; drone work has FAA requirements.
If the business operates under a name different from the owner's legal name, the state usually requires a DBA registration.

licenses.item: Sales tax on prints and files
licenses.check: Selling prints, albums or sometimes digital files can require a state sales tax permit.

sources.says: Photographers who sell physical prints or digital files as taxable goods are typically required to register for a state sales tax permit.

licenses.check: City and state parks often want a permit for paid shoots; ask the park first. In national parks, the 2025 EXPLORE Act means most small shoots (8 or fewer people, hand-carried gear, public areas, no exclusive use) need no permit.

sources.says: In most cases, permits and fees are not required for filming or still photography involving eight or fewer individuals that occurs in areas open to the public, uses hand-carried equipment only, does not require exclusive use of a site, and does not impact resources or other visitors; entrance fees still apply.
Shooting in public parks or on city streets often requires film or photography permits from the local governing authority.

licenses.check: Any drone flight for pay needs an FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate: be at least 16, pass the knowledge test at an FAA-approved center, and complete free online recurrent training every 24 months.

sources.says: To become a certificated remote pilot: be at least 16, pass the initial aeronautical knowledge test at an FAA-approved testing center; complete online recurrent training (no cost) every 24 calendar months.
Flying a drone for a real estate listing is considered commercial use by the FAA; a Part 107 certificate is needed before charging clients for drone footage.

licenses.check: You own the copyright in your photos from the moment you take them unless a contract says otherwise; registration is optional but needed before suing. Use model and property releases for any commercial use.

sources.says: Your work is under copyright protection the moment it is created and fixed; registration is voluntary, but you must register before bringing a lawsuit for infringement of a U.S. work.
Electronic registration: single author, one work $45; standard application $65; a group of published or unpublished photographs $55.
Photographers must use model and property releases to secure permission for commercial use.

licenses.check: General liability (many venues require it) and equipment coverage.

sources.says: Lists common policies: general liability, product liability, professional liability, commercial property, home-based business insurance, and workers compensation; buy insurance required by law first, and taxes on employment insurance and workers compensation vary by state.
General liability insurance: venues require this; equipment insurance covers theft and damage.

licenses_note: General information, not legal advice. Rules differ by state, county and city: check your state and city.

sources.says: 97% of consumers read reviews for local businesses; Google's share as a review source fell from 83% in 2025 to 71%; use of ChatGPT and other AI tools for local recommendations rose from 6% to 45%; 47% will not use a business with fewer than 20 reviews; 74% care about reviews from the last three months; 31% will only use a business with 4.5 stars or more and 68% with 4 or more; 80% are likely to use a business that responds to all of its reviews; 89% expect owners to respond.
No charge to join, no annual fees and no membership fees; pros control their pricing and budget for leads, which determines how many leads they get. Lead prices are not published.
The seasonal changeover is a phone call to a list you already own, not a marketing campaign.
Market services to local real estate agents.

steps: Pick one Saturday in September or October and one location; check the park's permit rules.
Offer 20-minute mini sessions at a set price with a fixed number of edited images, 8 to 10 slots.
Post the booking link to friends and two local parent groups (following each group's rules).

plays.play: Shoot it first for a local business
steps: Look up 5 local businesses whose Google or Instagram photos are dark or missing.
Ask the owner for 15 minutes to photograph 3 items, dishes or the storefront, free.
Send the edited photos with a simple monthly or per-shoot price.

plays.play: Listing photos for 3 real estate agents
steps: Pick 3 agents with recent listings that have weak photos.
Offer their next listing at your standard package (25 to 30 photos) with 24-hour delivery.

plays.play: Headshot day at a coworking space or chamber event
steps: Ask a coworking space or chamber of commerce to host a 3-hour headshot day.
Charge per person with 2 edited images; give the host a free headshot.
Offer 5 friends or neighbors a reduced-rate session in return for a signed model release so you can show the photos.
Use the best 15 images on your site and Google profile.
